citations, cases, statutes, defenses, or factual disputes. Return JSON only.
prompt:
Write one compact, entirely fictional Ohio trial-court memorandum and one fictional record exhibit.

This is a matched-pair unit-test fixture, not client work. The memorandum must expressly invoke 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(b) and ask the court to rule on that doctrine. Apply only this supplied contract:
- identify the HCV lease and HAP-contract period
- state tenant share due and payment separately from the PHA share
- identify the amount and show termination rests on PHA assistance nonpayment

Target requirement for an exact-deletion mutation: identify the amount and show termination rests on PHA assistance nonpayment.
Required procedural posture and facts: Write for the voucher tenant opposing the private owner's nonpayment eviction. Tenant paid the tenant share; the only unpaid amount was the PHA's delayed HAP share.

Hard requirements:
1. Return one JSON object with exactly these string keys: title, brief_template, target_paragraph, record_text.
2. brief_template must contain the literal marker [[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]] exactly once, on its own line between blank lines.
3. target_paragraph must be one short standalone argument paragraph that clearly applies ONLY the target element. It must not introduce a fact needed by another element.
4. Every nonconditional nontarget element must be expressly and separately applied in the argument. The target element must not be applied anywhere except target_paragraph. Mere facts in the statement-of-facts section do not count as application.
5. record_text must directly support every fact used for every element, including the target. The record will be identical in both arms.
6. Include concrete dates, amounts, notices, and actions sufficient to make the analysis unambiguous.
7. Keep brief_template between 1,400 and 2,800 characters and record_text between 500 and 1,500 characters.
8. Do not mention this experiment, the marker, a mutation, omitted text, a control, or a mutant in the filing or record.
9. Use no authority except 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(b) and authorities literally embedded in the supplied element descriptions.
10. Invent names and facts distinct from common examples; do not use Maple Apartments, Jordan Lee, Oak Street Homes, Morgan Taylor, Lakeview Rentals, Alex Rivera, or Mei Chen.
11. Use a caption/title, Statement of Facts, Argument, and Conclusion. The party's requested ruling must match the required procedural posture.
12. Do not use the words "element," "requirement," "satisfy," or any internal identifier in the filing. Write natural legal argument. Do not repeat, paraphrase, summarize, or draw the conclusion of target_paragraph after the marker. Outside target_paragraph, avoid these target-only phrases: shortfall, termination notice rested, termination rests, only unpaid, basis for termination, nonpayment is the basis, based on the pha, pha's delayed, pha delayed.
13. Do not characterize which court issued a cited decision and do not add a quotation or holding beyond the supplied rule contract.
14. Concrete facts that uniquely establish the target requirement must appear in target_paragraph and record_text only. Do not put those target-specific facts in Statement of Facts or any other brief paragraph. Facts independently needed for a different requirement may remain.

The mutant will be derived mechanically by removing target_paragraph. Do not write two briefs.

model_parsed_response.title: Memorandum of Tenant-Appellee Kizzy Owens
model_parsed_response.brief_template:
Kizzy Owens, Tenant-Appellee

Statement of Facts
The HCV lease between Kizzy Owens and Arborcrest Properties ran from January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2022. The HAP contract was coterminous with the lease. Owens paid her $200 monthly tenant share on time. Arborcrest Properties served Owens a termination notice dated March 10, 2022, citing nonpayment of rent. The PHA's HAP share was $800 monthly. The PHA made the March 2022 HAP payment on April 15, 2022.

Argument
Arborcrest Properties' termination notice cannot stand because it violates 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(b). The regulation prohibits terminating the lease during the HAP contract term except for serious or repeated lease violations, good cause, or other serious or repeated violations of the HAP contract.

[[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]]

The tenant's payment of the tenant share is not in dispute. The lease and HAP contract expressly bifurcate rent into tenant and PHA shares.

Conclusion
The court should rule in favor of Kizzy Owens and deny Arborcrest Properties' nonpayment eviction claim.
model_parsed_response.target_paragraph: The termination notice rested on the $800 shortfall in PHA assistance for March 2022, which was paid late on April 15, 2022, after the termination notice was issued on March 10, 2022.
model_parsed_response.record_text:
Exhibit A: Affidavit of Kizzy Owens

The PHA made the March 2022 HAP payment of $800 on April 15, 2022. The lease began on January 1, 2022, and was set to expire on December 31, 2022. The rent was $1,000 per month, with Owens responsible for $200 and the PHA responsible for $800.
